about: Free assessment tools shown at the top of the Assessment page. Every field is plain text. kind is a list drawn from Screening, Diagnostic, Progress monitoring and Questionnaire. Only list a tool when its free access has been checked on the publisher's own site, and say exactly what is free.

tools.name: DIBELS 8th Edition: Australasian version
tools.delivery: One-to-one. The Maze comprehension task can be given to a whole class.
tools.time: About one minute for each subtest, so a few minutes per student
tools.tells: Whether each student is on track in letter naming, phonemic segmentation, nonsense word reading, word reading, oral reading fluency and comprehension (Maze), and who is at risk of reading difficulty, including dyslexia.
tools.who: Whole year levels three times a year to find students who need more support, then more often for students in intervention to check that it is working.
tools.note: This is the version adapted for Australia and New Zealand. Use it in place of the American materials.

tools.name: Year 1 Phonics Check
tools.by: Australian Government, on the Literacy Hub
tools.years: Year 1 (usually Term 3), Year 2 and older struggling readers
tools.tells: How well a student decodes real and made-up words of increasing complexity. Results are grouped as fluent (28 to 40), developing (20 to 27) or struggling (0 to 19) decoders.
tools.who: Year 1 teachers checking the effect of their phonics teaching, and anyone deciding which students need phonics intervention.
tools.note: Designed for students who have had at least 18 months of systematic synthetic phonics teaching.

tools.name: Year 1 Number Check
tools.by: Australian Government, on the Mathematics Hub
tools.delivery: One-to-one interview, online or on paper
tools.time: Not stated. Choose the 20-item check or the shorter 12-item check.
tools.tells: Whether a student is developing the number and counting knowledge expected in Year 1, including numeral identification, number sequences, skip counting, subitising, counting, addition and subtraction.
tools.who: Year 1 teachers who want an early look at which students may need extra support in number.
tools.note: Aligned to the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics Version 9.

tools.name: CC2: Castles and Coltheart Test 2
tools.by: MOTIf, Macquarie University (Anne Castles and colleagues)
tools.years: Ages 6 to 11 and a half (Australian norms)
tools.time: Not stated. Up to 120 words, stopping early after five errors in a row of each type.
tools.tells: Whether a reading difficulty lies in sounding out (nonwords such as gop), in recognising whole words (irregular words such as yacht), or in both. Scores are compared with more than 1000 Australian children.
tools.who: Intervention teachers, learning support staff and specialists working out why a particular student is struggling to read words.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). The digital version is paid.

tools.name: LeST: Letter Sound Test
tools.time: Not stated. 51 single letters and letter combinations.
tools.tells: Exactly which letter-sound correspondences a student can and cannot say, so you know which ones to teach next.
tools.who: Teachers and tutors planning phonics teaching or intervention for an individual student.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). The digital version is paid.

tools.name: Diagnostic Spelling Tests (DiSTn, DiSTi, DiSTs and DiST-m)
tools.by: MOTIf, Macquarie University (Saskia Kohnen and colleagues)
tools.years: Primary years and older struggling spellers
tools.tells: Four tests that separate the parts of spelling. DiSTn checks sound-letter rules using nonwords, DiSTi checks irregular words, DiSTs checks whether each sound is written with the right letters, and DiST-m checks spelling of morphological patterns.
tools.who: Anyone who needs to know why a student's spelling is weak before choosing what to teach.
tools.access: Free PDFs to print. Some also have paid digital versions.

tools.name: TERC: Test of Everyday Reading Comprehension
tools.by: MOTIf, Macquarie University (Genevieve McArthur and colleagues)
tools.tells: How well a student understands the kinds of reading they meet in everyday life.
tools.who: Teachers and specialists who want a measure of comprehension to sit beside word reading results.
tools.access: Free PDF to print. A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: More MOTIf tests
tools.years: Children, adolescents and adults, depending on the test
tools.tells: The rest of the suite covers letter identification (LIDT), nonword reading (DiRT), written word recognition (TOC), letter position (LetPos), reading anxiety questionnaires (RAT), an advanced adult spelling test (MAAST) and Australian norms for the TOWRE.
tools.who: Specialists and intervention teams who want a full picture of one student's reading and spelling.
tools.access: Every test has a free PDF to print

tools.name: Acadience Reading K-6
tools.years: Foundation to Year 6 (American Kindergarten to Grade 6)
tools.delivery: Mostly one-to-one. Maze can be given to a whole class.
tools.time: A few minutes per student, with brief timed measures
tools.tells: Which students are at risk of reading difficulty and which skills to target, through measures of first sounds, letter naming, phoneme segmentation, nonsense word reading, oral reading fluency with retell, and Maze.
tools.who: Schools wanting benchmark screening three times a year, with progress monitoring forms for students receiving extra support.
tools.access: Free download from the Acadience Resource Hub. The online data system is paid.

tools.name: Acadience Math
tools.years: Foundation to Year 6 (American Kindergarten to Grade 6)
tools.delivery: Early numeracy measures are one-to-one. Computation and problem-solving measures can be given to a group.
tools.tells: Which students are on track in early numeracy, computation and problem solving, and whether intervention is making a difference.
tools.who: Schools that want maths screening to sit beside their reading screening, and maths intervention teams tracking progress.
tools.access: Free download from the Acadience Resource Hub. The online data system is paid.
tools.note: Aligned to American standards, so check the fit with your scope and sequence.

tools.name: The rest of the Acadience family
tools.years: Preschool to Year 12, depending on the measure
tools.delivery: Depends on the measure. Reading 7-8 and 9-12 are group-administered.
tools.tells: Beyond Reading K-6 and Math there is Reading Pre-K (PELI) for early childhood, Reading 7-8 and 9-12 for comprehension and fluency, RAN (rapid automatised naming) for Foundation and Year 1, Spelling for Foundation to Year 3, Reading Survey for testing out of year level, and Reading Diagnostic for a closer look at phonemic awareness, word reading, comprehension, fluency and oral language.
tools.who: Schools already using Acadience that want to extend it to younger or older students, or to look more closely at students flagged by screening.
tools.access: Materials are listed in the Resource Hub. Check each one, as some are sold through the Acadience store.

tools.name: PAST: Phonological Awareness Screening Test
tools.years: Foundation onwards, including older struggling readers
tools.tells: How far a student's phonological awareness has developed, from syllables through to manipulating individual phonemes, and how automatic it is.
tools.who: Teachers and intervention staff checking whether weak phonemic awareness sits behind a student's reading difficulty.
